claim: AI-assisted reverse engineering of legacy platforms using RAG and multi-agent orchestration reduced analysis-phase duration by 70-85% compared to manual reverse engineering, across multiple production engagements.
stance_target: automated codebase mastery / reverse engineering pillar delivers measurable throughput gains
scope_conditions: Dynamics Consulting legacy modernization engagements, published Nov 2025
quoted_support: Analysis speed: 70-85% reduction in time compared to manual reverse engineering

claim: A single named engagement (IATP) produced 47 functional specifications, a data dictionary covering 180+ database tables, and discovered 12 previously undocumented integration points with external systems, cutting the analysis phase from an estimated 3-4 months to under two weeks.
stance_target: concrete production evidence for AI-driven codebase reverse engineering at scale
scope_conditions: single named client engagement ('IATP'), Dynamics Consulting
quoted_support: In our IATP engagement, the reverse engineering phase produced 47 functional specifications, a complete data dictionary covering 180+ database tables, and a dependency map that revealed 12 undocumented integration points with external systems.

claim: AI-assisted codebase analysis consistently identifies 15-30% more integration points and business rules than manual human analysis, while maintaining a false-positive rate below 5% when paired with human validation.
stance_target: AI reverse engineering increases coverage without sacrificing accuracy when human-in-the-loop validation is retained
scope_conditions: aggregate across multiple Dynamics Consulting engagements
quoted_support: Coverage: AI-assisted analysis consistently identifies 15-30% more integration points and business rules than manual analysis. Accuracy: With human validation, the false positive rate on functional specifications is below 5%.

claim: Feeding an entire codebase to an LLM and requesting 'a complete analysis' without retrieval grounding produces confident-sounding but unreliable results: the model hallucinates nonexistent connections, misses real ones, silently ignores code paths outside its context window, and offers no traceability for verification.
stance_target: naive whole-codebase LLM prompting is sufficient for codebase mastery; the pillar requires grounding, not raw context stuffing
scope_conditions: legacy codebase analysis without RAG grounding
quoted_support: Feeding an entire codebase to an LLM and asking for 'a complete analysis' produces confident-sounding but unreliable results. Without retrieval grounding, the model hallucinates connections that do not exist and misses non-obvious ones that do.

claim: The production reverse-engineering pipeline uses domain-tuned code embeddings (not general-purpose text embeddings) and chunks the codebase at the function/method level with overlapping context windows to preserve call relationships, tagged with structural metadata (controller/service/model/utility) to enable filtered retrieval.
stance_target: technical architecture specification for the codebase-mastery pillar's RAG layer
quoted_support: The codebase is chunked at the function/method level, with overlapping context windows that preserve call relationships. Each chunk includes metadata: file path, module, language, and a structural tag (controller, service, model, utility).

claim: The multi-agent reverse-engineering workflow requires human-approval gates between each automated step (dependency mapper, data-flow tracer, business-rule extractor, API-surface analyser), with AI accelerating the work and humans validating it.
stance_target: human-in-the-loop checkpoints remain necessary even in autonomous agentic pipelines
scope_conditions: n8n-based multi-agent orchestration for codebase analysis
quoted_support: Each step produces artifacts that are reviewed by human analysts before the next step proceeds. The AI accelerates the work; humans validate it.

claim: An AI pipeline can quantify an 'obsolescence engine' pattern -- components where accumulated technical debt makes replacement cheaper than continued maintenance -- by measuring lines of dead code, unused dependencies, deprecated API calls, and security vulnerabilities in pinned library versions, providing an objective prioritization basis for modernization.
stance_target: automated technical-debt quantification as input to software-factory prioritization logic
quoted_support: The AI pipeline also identified the obsolescence engine pattern: components where technical debt had accumulated to the point where the cost of continued maintenance exceeded the cost of replacement. By quantifying this — lines of dead code, unused dependencies, deprecated API calls, security vulnerabilities in pinned library versions — the analysis provided an objective basis for prioritising which components to rebuild first.

claim: Total cost of AI-assisted legacy codebase analysis is typically 40-60% of the cost of equivalent manual analysis effort.
stance_target: cost optimization economics of the codebase-mastery pillar
quoted_support: Cost: Total cost of AI-assisted analysis is typically 40-60% of equivalent manual effort.
